rankings.blurb: Mahomes went for 30.48. Cam Skattebo added 30.0. Two players north of 30, and you didn't even need ARSB to carry the scoring this time — McCaffrey chipped in 20.6, Waddle contributed 13.32, and your 165.9 was the week's highest score for the second time in four weeks. The 58.24-point margin over Father Time was the biggest blowout of Week 6 until Ken-obi went and outdid everyone, but your 935.7 total points for leads the league by a comfortable margin over second place. Remember when the preseason said "since winning the inaugural title in 2022, you've been stuck in the middle"? At 5-1 with the most points in the Jailyard, the middle is a rearview mirror. Skattebo has emerged as a legitimate RB1 alongside McCaffrey, and Karim was in the chat this week pitching "2/3 top QBs come at me" like a man who knows his team is stacked. Next week brings General Ken-obi in a 5-1 versus 5-1 showdown that might determine bragging rights for the rest of the season. The Voltron receivers assembled. Now they need to survive the franchise that everyone measures themselves against.

The Rams defense scored 27.0 points. Let that sink in. Your best player this week was a team defense, and you still hung 164.94 on Burden in a 65.74-point blowout — the biggest margin of the entire week. Drake London went off for 26.8, Drake Maye added 26.24, and Rachaad White kicked in 16.1 in a performance so dominant that Jameson Williams' 15.6 barely cracked the conversation. The three-spot leap from fifth to second is the kind of correction that happens when you score 164.94 and the teams above you faceplant. Your Elo hit its all-time peak at 1700.2 — the highest rating in Jailyard history — and the all-time series against Burden moves to 3-2. The preseason said you were the franchise everyone measures themselves against. After a Week 4 stumble to Rasheeing and a quiet rebound in Week 5, this was the announcement game. Next week's matchup against the Legion is circled on every calendar in the league. Two 5-1 teams. Two former champions. One week to prove who belongs at the summit.

Four straight wins. Josh Jacobs bulldozed for 29.5, Jalen Hurts added 21.62, and Kyren Williams kept the wheels turning with 15.7 in a 129.82 cruise past Chudders. The all-time series is now 5-0 — you have never lost to Chudders Football Team, and at this point it's less of a stat and more of a restraining order. Derrick Henry's 13.5 kept producing from the RB3 slot, and the franchise with the league's best all-time record at 39-17 is quietly building a case for a return to the championship game. The preseason ranked you eleventh. You're third. Zach declared in the chat this week that "Ben's been my playoff kryptonite. Can't deny it. Comin for blood this year with my zombie wr corps." At 5-1 with the league's longest active winning streak, the zombies are alive, the kryptonite is irrelevant, and the Giants are the only team in the Jailyard that hasn't lost in October.

George Pickens went nuclear — 27.3 points. Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 26.2. That's 53.5 combined from your top two receivers in a 150.46-point performance that demolished Rasheeing the Scene by 41.36 and vaulted you from sixth to fourth. Joe Flacco — yes, that Joe Flacco — contributed 18.76 at quarterback while Maxx Crosby's 16.0 anchored the IDP slot. Your Elo jumped 25.9 points, the biggest gain of any team this week, and the all-time series against Rasheeing moves to 3-2. The preseason called you "the instigator of side bets and polls." This week you instigated a 41-point beatdown that left Patrick completely silent in the group chat. At 4-2 with the league's second-highest total points at 912.9, the aging core of Lamar, Tyreek, and Kelce still has a pulse — and Pickens plus JSN are proving the supporting cast isn't just wallpaper. The 0-5 career record against Kittler still haunts, but at least you're not the one dropping from first to fifth.

From the summit to the middle of the pack in seven days. MHJTIME's 140.94 steamrolled your 107.74, and the 33.2-point margin felt even worse because it came from a team you'd beaten four times in the all-time series. Jonathan Taylor's 21.7 and Baker Mayfield's 18.64 were fine — not great, fine — but your WR room combined for fewer points than Rico Dowdle scored by himself. Your Elo cratered 28.7 points, the steepest drop in the league this week, and the 202-point gap between your peak Elo of 1690.4 and your current mark of 1488.2 is starting to look less like a dip and more like a crater. The preseason called your ceiling "drywall." Last week, sitting at number one, we thought you'd smashed through it. This week the drywall smashed back. Runner-up in 2022, runner-up in 2023, champion in 2024, and now the fifth-ranked team in Week 6. Consistency is still the brand — it's just being consistently humbled right now.

De'Von Achane dropped 30.0 points and you still lost by 41.36. Read that again. Your best offensive weapon had a monster game, and the Boonist Monks beat you by more than most teams scored all week because Josh Allen — the consensus QB1 — managed only 15.4 and nobody else showed up behind Achane's heroics. Cameron Dicker's 18.4 from the kicker slot was your second-highest scorer, which tells you everything about how the rest of the roster performed. The silence in the group chat afterward was deafening — Patrick went from active chatter to completely MIA. The preseason called you "a weekly thrill ride." This was the part of the ride where the car derails. Your Elo dropped 25.9, and at 4-2 you're still in playoff position, but the WR room remains "a meme waiting to happen" and Allen having a pedestrian game exposed the uncomfortable truth: when Achane is the only one cooking, the kitchen still burns down.

Two weeks ago this column was writing your eulogy. Now you've won two straight by a combined 64.76 points, and the 140.94 you hung on the then-number-one Kittler might be the most meaningful win of your season so far. Rico Dowdle followed last week's 31.9 with 30.9 — the running back nobody had on preseason rosters is suddenly your most reliable weapon. Jayden Daniels added 22.64, Ja'Marr Chase contributed 20.1, and Trey McBride chipped in 17.2 from the TE slot. Your Elo surged 28.6 points, the second-biggest gain this week, and the "what if" franchise that was 1-3 now sits at .500 with a two-game streak. Nate was in the chat offering a $20 bet that Travis Hunter would outscore Kam Curl for the season. Brent's response — "Content is content. Production is production" — might as well be the motto for a team whose production is finally matching the content of its roster. The preseason said contender. The first four weeks said pretender. The last two weeks said: hold my Rico Dowdle.

Bijan Robinson. Thirty-two point eight. The week's top performer finally delivered the kind of game the preseason promised when it ranked you second overall. Caleb Williams added 19.88, Wan'Dale Robinson went for 17.4, and Tyler Warren's 15.3 gave you balanced production in a 151.88 outing that handled Ghastly by 30.58. The all-time series against Grayskull moves to 4-2, and your 3-3 record finally matches the roster's potential after an ugly start. Last week we asked "Where is Bijan Robinson? Where is A.J. Brown?" Bijan answered with a haymaker. Brown remains in the witness protection program. One half of the "league's scariest backfield" showed up — now you need the other half of the equation, the receivers, and the tight end room to follow suit. The preseason ranked you second. You're eighth. The real-life GM drafting style produced a real-life result this week, but one 32-point game from Bijan doesn't erase five weeks of the supporting cast treating production like a suggestion.

Back-to-back losses. Last week you fell to a 0-4 Chudders team by 2.02. This week Noble FFT handled you by 30.58. D'Andre Swift's 24.5 and DK Metcalf's 17.5 weren't enough when your scoring ceiling capped at 121.3 — your second-lowest output of the season. Brian Burns' 17.0 from the DE slot was solid, but when a defensive end is outscoring most of your offensive starters, the blueprint needs revising. Your Elo dropped 16.0, and the two-game skid has you at 2-4 and sinking after the 176.42 explosion in Week 4 felt like a turning point. Oscar was active in the chat this week — mostly roasting other teams — but at 2-4, the jokes are starting to land on the wrong side. The preseason said "picks don't score points." Right now neither do your starters, and the Week 4 performance against Kittler looks more like an outlier than a floor.

Matt accidentally dropped Haskins on the Sleeper app this week. "There's absolutely no way in my right mind I meant to drop Haskins," he told the chat, followed by "Swear to god this app glitched." The league's reaction? Zach: "Mwahahahaha what a great sight that was to wake up to." Brent immediately put in a waiver bid. It's been that kind of season. Your 95.26 was the lowest score in the league this week, with Justin Herbert's 18.76 leading and Jared Verse's 17.5 from the DL slot as your second-best performer. Ashton Jeanty managed 15.6, Jahmyr Gibbs regressed to 7.0, and the first-win celebration from last week feels like it happened in a different timeline. The rebuild is still the plan, the war chest is still enormous, and 2026 is still the target. But at 1-5 with the second-fewest total points in the league at 727.9, the lumps aren't just landing — they're leaving marks.

Six weeks. Zero wins. And this time there's no moral victory to cling to — Ken-obi's 164.94 steamrolled your 99.2 by 65.74 in the biggest blowout of the week. Byron Young led your scoring at 21.0 from the LB slot. Your quarterback, Tua Tagovailoa, posted 9.6. When your IDP linebacker outscores your quarterback by more than double, the roster construction isn't broken — it's demolished. Harlow was pitching "2 of the top 3 RBs on the Chiefs" in the trade chat this week, and the desperation is justified. The all-time series against Ken-obi moves to 2-3, your Elo sank another 10.3 to 1323.5, and the preseason called you "a cautionary tale of stars without support." Six weeks in, the tale has become a saga. Next week brings Father Time — also 0-6 — in a game that absolutely nobody asked for but everyone needs. Someone will get their first win. Do whatever it takes to make sure it's you.

The lowest-scoring team in the league just absorbed a 58.24-point loss to the highest-scoring team. Ladd McConkey's 19.5 and Tetairoa McMillan's 16.4 provided flickers — the wagyu beef WRs at least showed up to the grill — but Bo Nix's 13.36 at quarterback and Aidan Hutchinson's 9.0 from the DL slot weren't close to enough against a Legion team that had two players above 30. Your Elo dropped 14.8, your total points for sits at 712.7 — last in the league — and the preseason's prediction of "spoiler potential" has been replaced by a simpler label: punching bag. Next week brings Burden in the 0-6 Bowl, and the matchup might be the most important game neither team wants to acknowledge. Somebody will get win number one. Somebody will go to 0-7. The chat will probably ignore both outcomes entirely — and honestly, can you blame them?

confessionals.text: I was number one for exactly one week. One glorious, deceiving week. Then MHJTIME showed up with Rico Dowdle's 30.9 and knocked me all the way to fifth. Jonathan Taylor gave me 21.7 and it wasn't enough. Baker gave me 18.64 and it wasn't enough. Nothing was enough. I went from defending champion at the top of the mountain to defending champion wondering where the mountain went. The chat hasn't said a word to me about it. Somehow that's worse.

Three weeks ago this column called my season a 'what if' story headed for the toilet bowl. I screenshot'd that paragraph. I printed it out. It's on my desk right now, next to my two-game winning streak and the scoreboard that says 140.94 against the number one team. Ja'Marr Chase remembered he's Ja'Marr Chase. Rico Dowdle — a guy I almost benched — scored 30.9 for the second straight week. The 'what if' franchise just became the 'what now' franchise.

So the Sleeper app may have glitched and I may have accidentally dropped Haskins. The entire group chat saw it before I could fix it. Zach said it was 'a great sight to wake up to.' Brent immediately put in his waiver bid. And then we scored 95.26, the lowest in the league. Last week I was celebrating our first win with champagne. This week I'm back to pouring it out.

I don't say much in the group chat. I don't need to. The Rams defense scored 27 for me. Drake London went for 26.8. Drake Maye added 26.24. We put up 164.94 and won by 65.74 — the biggest blowout of the week. My Elo just hit its all-time peak. And next week I get the Legion of Bouz, first versus second. I haven't typed a single word in the chat about it. I'm just loading the lineup.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: The Lock of the Week has now busted three weeks in a row. Is it cursed?
mailbag.answer: Three straight Lock losses. At this point the Lock isn't a prediction — it's a hex. Kittler was -4.0 at home against a 2-3 MHJTIME team that proceeded to drop 140.94. The cumulative record is 18-12, which is still respectable, but the Lock specifically is 0-3 over the last three weeks. We're not retiring it — we're just warning you: whatever the Lock picks next week, bet the other side.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: Legion of Bouz versus General Ken-obi next week. Both 5-1. Who ya got?
mailbag.answer: The matchup has everything: two former champions with matching trophy cases, Mahomes versus Maye, the league's highest scorer versus the league's highest Elo. Ken-obi's 1700.2 Elo is the best in the Jailyard. Legion's 935.7 total points is the best in the Jailyard. Something's got to give — and we're not dumb enough to make it the Lock.

mailbag.question: @ToreroGaucho asks: Achane scored 30.0 and I still lost by 41. What am I supposed to do?
mailbag.answer: Score more points from the other positions. When your kicker is your second-highest scorer at 18.4, the problem isn't Achane — it's everyone who isn't Achane. Josh Allen at 15.4 is the real villain. The preseason QB1 needs to QB1.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: Both Burden and Father Time are 0-6 and play each other next week. What's the over/under on combined score?
mailbag.answer: Burden averages 122.1 per week. Father Time averages 118.8. Combined that's about 241, but I'll set the line at 220.5 because neither team has given us reason to trust their floor. The real question isn't the over/under — it's whether the group chat will even notice the game is happening.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: Ben said Zach's WRs are '2nd place also rans' compared to his 'championship pedigree' receivers. Whose WRs are actually better?
mailbag.answer: Ben's Kittler just dropped 107.74 with WR production you'd need a microscope to find. Zach's Giants are 5-1 with a four-game winning streak and Josh Jacobs doing the heavy lifting. Championship pedigree is great for trash talk. Four straight wins is great for the standings. Advantage: zombies.

bits.title: Preseason Prediction Tracker
bits.text: Week 5 picks went 4-2, bringing the cumulative record to 18-12. The Lock of the Week (Kittler -4.0 over MHJTIME) busted for the third consecutive week — MHJTIME won 140.94 to 107.74. The Upset Watch (Noble FFT +1.0 over Ghastly) hit — Noble won 151.88-121.3 behind Bijan Robinson's 32.8. The Lock is now 0-3 over the last three weeks. Still profitable overall, but the signature pick has become a signature jinx.

bits.title: Overheard in the Chat
bits.text: The week's best exchange: Zach offered 'Buncha old serviceable WR3/4s here. Hit me up.' Ben responded: 'If you want some old serviceable WR3/4s with championship pedigree instead of Zach's 2nd place also rans, let me know.' Brent narrated: 'Zach got served by Ben.' Ben's follow-up — 'Too soon?' — was the chef's kiss. Zach's rebuttal: 'Ben's been my playoff kryptonite. Can't deny it. Comin for blood this year with my zombie wr corps.' At 5-1, the zombies are winning the argument.

bits.title: IDP Monster of the Week
bits.text: The Los Angeles Rams defense — or should we say General Ken-obi's defense — scored 27.0 points, outscoring most offensive starters across the league. Byron Young (21.0 for Burden), Jared Verse (17.5 for Chudders), and Brian Burns (17.0 for Ghastly) all had strong IDP weeks, but a team defense hanging 27 in an IDP league is borderline unfair.

bits.title: Things I Believe But Can't Prove
bits.text: MHJTIME will make the playoffs. The Lock of the Week will hit next week specifically because we've acknowledged the curse. Kittler won't drop below sixth all season. The Burden-Father Time game next week will be the lowest-scoring game of the year. And someone in the group chat already screenshot'd this column's Lock prediction, ready to roast us when it inevitably busts again.

bits.title: Is MHJTIME the New 2024 Sleeping Giants?
bits.text: Last season, the Sleeping Giants started slow, caught fire mid-season, and rode the momentum all the way to the championship game. MHJTIME was 1-3, looked dead, and has now won two straight by a combined 64.76 points with Rico Dowdle emerging as an unexpected weapon. Different roster, same trajectory. If Week 7 brings a third straight win against Chudders, the parallel becomes undeniable.

picks.blurb: The Monks just dropped 150.46 with Pickens and JSN combining for 53.5, and the scoring machine that leads the league's second-highest total PF at 912.9 should handle a Noble squad that's been maddeningly inconsistent. Bijan Robinson's 32.8 was a revelation, but one week doesn't fix a pattern of underperformance from the supporting cast.

Kittler just fell from first to fifth, and the Sleeping Giants are riding the league's longest winning streak at four games. Josh Jacobs' 29.5 and Jalen Hurts' 21.62 give the Giants a dependable floor, but the defending champion has historically bounced back from adversity. This one's closer than the records suggest.

The 0-6 Bowl. Somebody has to win. Burden has slightly more total points (732.7 vs 712.7) and Byron Young's 21.0 IDP performance suggests a higher ceiling, but Father Time has McConkey, McMillan, and the occasional Bo Nix eruption. This is genuinely unpredictable, and the group chat will probably not watch.

The game of the season. Legion leads the league in total points at 935.7. Ken-obi leads the league in Elo at 1700.2. Mahomes versus Maye. McCaffrey versus Barkley. Two former champions, two titles each. Ken-obi's Elo edge and 164.94-point statement this week tilt the needle — barely. We absolutely refuse to make this the Lock.

Rasheeing got demolished by the Monks this week, but Josh Allen and Achane at full strength are still one of the most explosive duos in the league. Ghastly has lost two straight and can't find consistency beyond isolated explosion games. The 4-2 team with the better quarterback handles the 2-4 team searching for answers.

Yes, the Lock has busted three straight weeks. Yes, picking the Lock is essentially hexing the favorite. But MHJTIME just dropped 140.94 on the number one team, Rico Dowdle is averaging 30.9 over the last two weeks, and Chudders just put up the lowest score of the week at 95.26. If this Lock busts, we're shutting the feature down permanently. We mean it. Probably.
